Hyperparameter Derivatives of a Penalty

Source: R/generics.R
penalty_grad_theta.Rd

The three functions return the three blocks of derivatives in the hyperparameters. penalty_grad_theta() returns \(\partial\rho/\partial\theta_k\), penalty_hess_theta() returns \(\partial^2\rho/\partial\theta_k\partial\theta_l\), and penalty_cross() returns the mixed block \(\partial^2\rho/\partial\beta\,\partial\theta_k\), one coefficient vector per hyperparameter. Each is returned on the parameter scale or on the unconstrained scale, as selected by scale.

Usage

penalty_grad_theta(penalty, beta, theta, scale = c("parameter", "link"), ...)

penalty_hess_theta(penalty, beta, theta, scale = c("parameter", "link"), ...)

penalty_cross(penalty, beta, theta, scale = c("parameter", "link"), ...)

Arguments

penalty

A penalty() object of any branch.

beta

A finite numeric vector of length penalty@n_coef, coerced with as.numeric() in the generic. A vector of another length signals an error.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector carrying the same, holding every name in penalty@params.

scale

"parameter", the default, gives derivatives in \(\theta\). "link" gives them in the unconstrained values \(\eta = g(\theta)\), which is the scale on which an optimizer works and on which a hyperparameter's standard error is built.

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not read it.

Value

All three return a named list. penalty_grad_theta() has one element per hyperparameter; each element is a single number, and the elements are named by penalty@params. penalty_hess_theta() has \(p(p+1)/2\) elements; each element is a single number, and the elements are keyed by pairs as described above. penalty_cross() has one element per hyperparameter; each element is a numeric vector of length penalty@n_coef.

Uses of the three blocks

The gradient and the Hessian in \(\theta\) are the steps of a joint maximization over coefficients and hyperparameters, and the quantities that are differentiated in the Laplace term of a marginal criterion. The mixed block is the off-diagonal corner of that joint system, and it also enters the implicit function theorem: the penalized mode moves with a hyperparameter as \(\partial\hat\beta/\partial\theta_k = -(H + S)^{-1} \partial^2\rho/\partial\beta\,\partial\theta_k\), so the derivative of a criterion computed at the mode requires it.

The two scales

Each hyperparameter carries a link \(g\) that maps its open interval onto the whole line. If scale = "link", the derivatives are taken in \(\eta = g(\theta)\), the coordinates that an unconstrained optimizer moves. The chain rule is applied in the generic body, so a method always returns the parameter scale and a branch written by a user obtains both scales without further code. Writing \(h = g^{-1}\),

$$\frac{\partial\rho}{\partial\eta_k} = \frac{\partial\rho}{\partial\theta_k} h_k'(\eta_k), \qquad \frac{\partial^2\rho}{\partial\eta_k \partial\eta_l} = \frac{\partial^2\rho}{\partial\theta_k \partial\theta_l} h_k'(\eta_k) h_l'(\eta_l) + \delta_{kl} \frac{\partial\rho}{\partial\theta_k} h_k''(\eta_k),$$

and the mixed block picks up one factor of \(h_k'\) and no second-order term, because a reparametrization of the hyperparameters does not change the coefficient direction.

Names of the elements

The gradient and the mixed block are keyed by penalty@params. The Hessian is keyed by pairs. The diagonal entries come first, in params order, the upper off-diagonal pairs follow, and each key joins the two names with an underscore. For an elastic net the keys are lambda_lambda, alpha_alpha, lambda_alpha. Only the upper triangle is returned, since the matrix is symmetric.

See also

penalty_value() for the quantity differentiated, penalty_gradient() for the coefficient derivatives, penalty_dhessian() for the third-order blocks that a marginal criterion reads, check_penalty() to verify all three against numerical routes.

Examples

pen <- quadratic_penalty(diag(2))
penalty_grad_theta(pen, c(1, -1), list(lambda = 3))
#> $lambda
#> [1] 0.6666667
#> 
penalty_hess_theta(pen, c(1, -1), list(lambda = 3))
#> $lambda_lambda
#> [1] 0.1111111
#> 
penalty_cross(pen, c(1, -1), list(lambda = 3))
#> $lambda
#> [1]  1 -1
#> 

# An elastic net has two hyperparameters, so three Hessian keys.
enet <- elasticnet_penalty(n_coef = 3)
names(penalty_hess_theta(enet, c(1, -0.4, 0.2),
                         list(lambda = 2, alpha = 0.4)))
#> [1] "lambda_lambda" "alpha_alpha"   "lambda_alpha" 

# The link scale is the parameter scale times the chain factor. lambda
# rides a log link, so h'(eta) is lambda itself.
g_par  <- penalty_grad_theta(pen, c(1, -1), list(lambda = 3))
g_link <- penalty_grad_theta(pen, c(1, -1), list(lambda = 3),
                             scale = "link")
all.equal(g_link$lambda, g_par$lambda * 3)
#> [1] TRUE
